purpose: Paper replication failures that have been investigated and are kept as failures. Each is bound to its case definition, frozen target and tolerance, and the value it fails with; the audit accepts it only while the observed value stays within the regression bound. Targets are never changed here.
regression_basis: The engine is deterministic for a given image; the observed values were reproduced bit for bit across runs.

failures.finding: FEMM's 2D phase inductance with the stated magnet permeability 1.22 is 3.5% above the paper's 2D FEA value. With unit magnet permeability it is 1.1607 mH, within 0.06%; the paper's 14 mm effective air gap (magnet depth plus gap) also implies unit permeability, so the paper's FEA most likely treated the magnets as air.

Where stator and rotor poles overlap, FEMM's phase flux linkage exceeds the paper's FEM curves (Fig. 8) by a factor that depends on rotor position but not on current: the paper's values are 0.973, 0.967 and 0.961 times the model's at 15, 20 and 30 degrees from 4 to 18 A, while unaligned and at 10 degrees they agree within 0.0003 and 0.0043 Wb. The mesh is converged, and the geometry, coil, steel and air-gap controls each change the curves' shape rather than scaling them, so no input the case varies explains the excess; a pole-flux evaluation is ruled out by the unaligned agreement. The cause is open.
related: controls mesh-0p6, table-bore-reading, rotor-root-from-height, parallel-rotor-poles, coil-blocks-diagonal-reading, steel-hot-rolled, air-gap-0p42

failures.finding: Every phase voltage per turn is the table's value times 1.4135-1.4138 (sqrt 2 = 1.4142): the model's voltage assessor reports the peak magnitude of the phasor, and Tables I and III give rms voltages. The torques and losses fix the current as 310 A/cm^2 rms; with 310 A/cm^2 read as the amplitude (control current-density-amplitude-310) every voltage agrees within 0.05% but every torque and loss is halved. The frozen voltage targets compare a peak with an rms value; they stay as frozen.

Two of 24 flux-linkage targets miss Motor-CAD's maps (File S5) narrowly: psi_d at no load is 2.86% low (0.00215 Wb against a 0.002 Wb tolerance) and psi_q at (0, 100 A) 1.23% high (0.00204 Wb). The mesh is converged (0.7 times moves each by under 0.15 mWb) and the shaft does not matter. Solid steel worsens both (-3.99% and +4.22%). Magnets at 20 C instead of the frozen 40 C bring both within tolerance but move psi_d at (0, 200 A) from +0.04% to +2.83%, so magnet temperature does not explain the map as a whole. The maps are interpolations between Motor-CAD FE points whose conditions the paper does not state. Inputs stay as frozen.

The initial design and five further designs agree with the analytic stall torques within 1%, but 16/3 is 3.07% low and Table 3's Designs 1, 4 and 5 about 1.3% low and Design 2 2.39% high. The mesh is converged (0.7 times moves the torques by 0.1%), the iron is effectively infinitely permeable (ten times more moves them 0.07%), and the rounding of Table 3's variables moves them by at most 0.3%. 16/3 is also the one combination below the paper's own FEM, and Design 2's stated PM mass is 4% off the others. The causes are open; inputs and targets stay as frozen.

The inner bar's skin factors at 50 Hz, k_ri = 4.81 and k_xi = 0.932, miss the text's 2.36 and 0.955, but those text values belong to the paper's approximate circuit: its Fig. 8 plots the FE skin factors, which read 4.77 and 0.931 at 50 Hz. The case froze the text values as FE skin factors; they stay frozen. The inner bar's DC self-inductance is 1.01% high (6.569 against 6.503 uH/m), with all three inductances 0.6-1.0% high and the mesh converged (halving it moves them under 0.06%); Fig. 1's dimensions are printed to 0.1 mm.

Every torque is 27-36% above the paper's (Table 3 at rated current, Fig. 11 at 2/3 of it) by a nearly uniform factor: the torque-angle curve's shape matches within 1.1% and the factor is the same at both currents, so saturation and the d/q ratio are reproduced and the magnitude is not. No control moves the torque by more than 3.2% (rib, barrier ends, steel, shaft, tooth tips, mesh); reading 22 A as the amplitude undershoots by 23% and distorts the curve. A uniform factor behaves like an effective length (about 106 of the 140 mm stack), which the paper does not state. The cause is open; inputs and targets stay as frozen.
related: controls rib-0p8, barrier-ends-full-width, steel-m45, shaft-steel, shoe-depth-1p2, current-amplitude-22, mesh-0p7

failures.finding: The 2D torque at 3 A rms passes from beta = 0 to 50 degrees but is 1.16% high at 60 and 1.74% high at 80. The model's d-axis inductance is 2.1% below Table 1's (q-axis 0.5% below); a larger Lq - Ld adds reluctance torque, which grows with beta. Flux-linkage and stress-tensor torques agree within 0.03%, mesh 0.7 moves torque by 0.1%, and no assumed input (stacking factor, shaft and bolt materials, depth) closes the gap without failing the flux target.
related: controls mesh-0p7, stacking-factor-1, depth-rotor-length, shaft-steel, holes-steel

failures.finding: Example 1 is within 0.64 N m of Fig. 12's FEM points (rms 0.44 N m on a 74 N m curve, fundamental +0.6%), failing five of 13 points at the 1% tolerance. Example 2's fundamental and 3rd harmonic agree with Fig. 17's points (40.46 against 40.39 N m) but its 45th and 51st order ripple is in antiphase with them, so the points alternate between +27.5% and -10.8%. A meshed-gap diagnostic agrees with the sliding band within 0.6% and mesh 0.6 moves results by 0.2%, so the construction is not the cause; the relative angle of the outer magnets and pole pieces, which the paper does not state, could be.

Fig. 19's static torque contradicts Fig. 10 and the stated currents: with phase A's EMF largest at 0 degrees, Ia = I and Ib = Ic = -I/2 give the largest torque there, where Fig. 19 is zero. With the current phasor turned 270 electrical degrees (Ia = 0, Ib = -Ic = -(sqrt 3/2) I) the same model reproduces Fig. 19's 38 FEM points within 0.069 N m rms at the stated peak current; moving the rotor origin instead fits no better than 2.4 N m. No load passes.

Fig. 18's static torque is zero at the sweep's start, which the stated currents and the model's rotor reference do not give (8.8 N m there). An exact scan over current phase for both slot readings (the model is linear) fits Fig. 18 at best within 1.24 N m rms (frozen slots) or 0.91 N m (half-slot reading, -12.5 degrees), against 13.5 and 4.4 at the stated phase; the assumed slot positions move the load torque by up to 97%. The cause is open; the EMF passes.
